Before versus after

These bars count actual sampled training targets, before and after introducing antenna-to-terrain window preferences. Blue is the previous uniform eligible-edge sampler; orange is the new sampler. Both use 1,446,106 unique profiles and 20,682,097 training rows across depths 100–1,000 m. Each profile contributes the same number of rows at each depth in both versions. Only the target selection changes.

The charts show 100–500 m prediction depths, where sampling changes. AGL is target height above the radar’s minimum-terrain proxy (asl.min); it is distinct from prediction depth below the observed profile. Bins are 100 m wide. The existing 1 m terrain tolerance is included in the lowest band.

By prediction depth

How the preference is calculated

For each training-site profile, its naturally lowest measured bin defines the observed edge. The desired targets are 100–500 m below that edge, within the station’s antenna-to-asl.min window and above the terrain floor. No measurement below the antenna is required to define demand. Measured donor targets at matching AGL/depth combinations supply training labels, potentially from other radars.

Within each depth, let \(q_{bk}\) be the desired share in AGL band \(b\), averaged equally over contributing training radars, and \(p_{bk}\) its share among all eligible measured donor targets. The preference is

\[ a_{bk}=\min\{5,q_{bk}/p_{bk}\},\qquad p_{bk}>0. \]

For remaining eligible edges \(E_{ik}\) in profile \(i\), each draw uses

\[ P(e\mid i,k)=\frac{0.25}{|E_{ik}|} +0.75\frac{a_{b(e),k}}{\sum_{e'\in E_{ik}}a_{b(e'),k}}. \]

If all remaining preferences are zero, sampling is uniform. Draw up to three distinct edges without replacement. The cap of 5 applies to the raw preference, not the final probability ratio. Limited eligible edges can restrict how much the realized distribution changes. Unsupported demand does not create synthetic labels.

Controlled comparison

Whole-profile and observed-upper VID remain ≥6.6 birds/km². Features, VID fitting weights, radar-night/site/year splits and frozen evaluation rows are retained. Depths 600–1,000 m retain their original sampling. The model uses raw-density stopping: the arithmetic mean of depth-specific RMSE at 100–500 m, with a 20,000-round ceiling and patience 300. The control is the earlier unsmoothed model selected at 3,989 rounds.

These plots describe data preparation, not evidence of improved predictions. Model performance will be evaluated on the same held-out rows. Naturally missing lower layers still lack direct ground truth.

Reproduce from analysis/window-sampling/: run Rscript render.R. The four sampling CSVs and audit JSON alongside report.Rmd record the exact counts and provenance. Run identifier: conus-depth1to10-window-20261009-01.
